turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hello, Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you too. 

Well, I came in because I just can’t seem to get anything in order anymore. It's getting to be a real problem. Right now, my kitchen table is completely covered with my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, notes from the senior center, and all these half-finished lists. I'll sit down there, and I just don't know which thing to do first... and I end up just sitting there looking at it until the whole day is gone.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly states an inability to get things in order, describing a cluttered table and half-finished lists.
symptom_reasoning.S031: The patient describes severe indecisiveness, stating they sit at the table not knowing what to do first until the whole day passes.

turns.doctor_question: Have you struggled with this kind of difficulty focusing or organizing your tasks your whole life, or is this a relatively new problem for you?
turns.patient_response: Well, honestly, it's been my whole life. Even back when I was a little girl, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. I was always forgetting my books and my homework... and I always needed constant reminders to just finish my seatwork before I could go outside to play. So, yes, it's always been this way, it just feels like it's getting harder to manage now.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often feel like you have an inner restlessness, or do you find it difficult to sit still for long periods of time?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I do. I mean, even when I’m really trying to just sit politely in a meeting or a group, I can't quite seem to do it.
